tagline: River crossings trace changing roads and a town moved upriver
intro: The Cottage Grove Covered Bridge Tour links river crossings in town with bridges near Walden and Dorena Reservoir. Oregon’s Department of Transportation includes it in its scenic-byway collection as a 20-mile tour route, with a minimum driving time of one to two hours. Its seven bridges include the Swinging Bridge, a suspension footbridge, alongside the covered spans. At Mosby Creek, the single lane of the 1920 bridge still carries traffic.

These crossings served different journeys: lumberman J.E. Chambers built his railroad bridge in 1925 to connect a sawmill with timberlands west of town. Dorena Bridge followed in 1949 after construction of the dam, tying together roads on the lake’s north and south sides. The reservoir flooded the old Dorena townsite, and the community moved five miles upriver. Later restoration changed the crossings again: Chambers was rebuilt in 2011 for pedestrians and cyclists, while Dorena Bridge became a wedding site.

Begin in Cottage Grove, where the rebuilt Chambers bridge now serves walkers and cyclists. Continue to the Walden area for Mosby Creek Bridge and to Currin Bridge on the Row River. East of Cottage Grove lies Dorena Lake; Dorena Bridge crosses the river near the reservoir’s upper end. Beyond the old flooded site, the relocated community of Dorena completes the journey upriver.

moments.title: Mosby Creek Bridge
moments.text: Mosby Creek Bridge carries traffic through a covered crossing built in 1920, the oldest covered bridge in Lane County. It takes its name from David Mosby, who settled on a 1,600-acre land claim near the present crossing east of Cottage Grove. Walter and Miller Sorensen built it for $4,125. Its entrances have semicircular arches, with ribbon openings along the roofline and board-and-batten siding outside. The bridge underwent a major restoration in 1990, followed in 2002 by replacement of its corrugated metal roof with synthetic material. Its one lane remains open to vehicles.
moments.notice: Look for semicircular entrances, narrow openings at the roofline and board-and-batten siding.

moments.title: Currin Bridge
moments.text: White entrances and red sides give Currin Bridge its two-color exterior above the Row River. The 1925 crossing replaced an 1883 covered bridge built by Nels Roney. In 1979, Lane County finished a concrete bridge nearby and closed the covered bridge to road traffic. The concrete crossing stands only a few feet away. Structural repairs followed in 1987, and a grant supported further restoration in 1993–1995. The bridge uses a Howe truss and entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1979. Lane County’s Oregon Covered Bridge Program received $48,000 toward the later restoration.
moments.notice: The covered span has white portals and red sides; the newer concrete bridge is only a few feet away.

moments.title: Dorena Bridge
moments.text: Dorena Bridge was built for a landscape newly changed by a dam. Constructed in 1949, it linked the roads on the north and south sides of Dorena Lake. The covered span crosses 105 feet of the Row River near the reservoir’s upper end. It was restored in 1996. With road traffic removed, the crossing has taken on another use: ODOT identifies it as a popular wedding site.

moments.title: Dorena
moments.text: Dorena’s present location is five miles upriver from the townsite flooded by its namesake reservoir. Before the move, Dorena had a school built in 1896 and a post office established in 1899, both predating the reservoir project. The old town was abandoned in 1946 as the Corps of Engineers began building Dorena Dam for flood control. The Corps relocated approximately one hundred homes before the dam’s completion in 1949. The Row River Trail now passes through Dorena on a former railway corridor. That line belonged to the Oregon, Pacific and Eastern Railway.

practical: Dorena Bridge: Dorena Bridge is closed to vehicle traffic. (checked 2026-10-11)
